Expected Cross-Validation Index (ECVI) for a Covariance-Structure Model

Source: R/ecvi.R
ecvi.Rd

The ECVI of Browne and Cudeck (1989) estimates how well a fitted model's implied covariance matrix would fit an independent sample of the same size from the same population. It is the single-sample estimate of the cross-validation discrepancy, so a smaller ECVI indicates a model expected to generalize better; ECVI is most useful for comparing competing models fit to the same data. A confidence interval, derived from the noncentral chi square distribution, accompanies the point estimate.

Usage

ecvi(
  fit = NULL,
  chisq = NULL,
  df = NULL,
  npar = NULL,
  multiplier = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted lavaan model. Supply this, or the summary statistics below.

chisq, df, npar

The model chi square, its degrees of freedom, and the number of free parameters. Used when fit is not supplied, so an ECVI can be obtained from a published fit table.

multiplier

The multiplier with which the chi square was formed from the minimized fit function, which is the divisor of the ECVI (\(n\) in Details): the total sample size \(N\) for a statistic formed as \(N\hat{F}\), and \(N - G\) for \(G\) groups for a statistic formed as \((N - G)\hat{F}\). Given with chisq, df, and npar when fit is not supplied; with a fitted model it is taken from the fit.

conf_level

Confidence level for the interval. Defaults to 0.95.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with rows ecvi, ci_lower, and ci_upper in the value column.

Details

With \(q\) free parameters, \(\mathrm{ECVI} = (\chi^2 + 2q)/n\), where \(n\) is the multiplier with which the chi square was formed from the minimized fit function (the argument multiplier), \(\chi^2 = n\hat{F}\), so that \(\mathrm{ECVI} = \hat{F} + 2q/n\) (Browne & Cudeck, 1989). With a fitted model the divisor is the one lavaan uses, and the value is the one lavaan::fitMeasures() reports: \(n = N\), the total sample size, for maximum likelihood under lavaan's default normal likelihood (including MLR, whose unscaled statistic is used, and FIML), and \(n = N - G\) for \(G\) groups under likelihood = "wishart" and for the least squares estimators (GLS, WLS, ULS, DWLS). With summary statistics, multiplier is used as given: pass \(N - G\) when the published chi square was formed as \((N - G)\hat{F}\), as by programs that follow the Wishart convention. Writing \(\hat\lambda = \chi^2 - df\) for the estimated noncentrality, the ECVI is \((\hat\lambda + df + 2q)/n\); the confidence interval replaces \(\hat\lambda\) by the lower and upper noncentrality limits from ci_nc_chisq, the same inversion used for the RMSEA interval (see ci_rmsea).

The noncentrality limits are at least 0, while the point estimate is the untruncated \(\hat{F} + 2q/n\) of Browne and Cudeck (1989), so for a model with \(\chi^2 < df\) the estimate lies below the lower limit, \((df + 2q)/n\). When the chi square lies at or below the upper \(\alpha/2\) quantile of the central chi square distribution, for \(\alpha\) = 1 - conf_level, the lower noncentrality limit is 0 and the lower limit is that same \((df + 2q)/n\). When it lies at or below the lower \(\alpha/2\) quantile, no noncentrality is consistent with it at that level, and the upper limit is NA, with a warning. sem_fit_measures reports the upper RMSEA limit as 0 in that case, so that it agrees with the test of not close fit, but the ECVI has no such test, and an upper limit of \((df + 2q)/n\) would make an interval of zero width that excludes the estimate.

A fitted model must have converged to an admissible solution, as for sem_fit_measures: a solution with a negative variance estimate, or with a covariance matrix of the latent variables, of the residuals of the observed variables, or of the structural residuals that is not positive definite, is refused (with an error of class dmar_inadmissible), since its fit describes estimates outside the parameter space; with auxiliary variables the check is made on the model's own parameters.

When the chi square is the likelihood ratio statistic \(2(\ell_s - \ell_M)\), as under lavaan's default normal likelihood, \(N \cdot \mathrm{ECVI} = \mathrm{AIC} + 2\ell_s\), where \(\ell_s\) is the maximized log likelihood of the saturated model and \(\ell_M\) that of the fitted model. ECVI and AIC then rank models fitted to the same data identically, and their values differ only by the saturated log likelihood constant before division by \(N\). Under the Wishart convention the statistic is \((N - G)/N\) times the likelihood ratio statistic, and the identity holds only approximately. ECVI is reported because its metric (a discrepancy per observation) and its confidence interval are interpretable on their own.

References

Browne, M. W., & Cudeck, R. (1989). Single sample cross-validation indices for covariance structures. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 24(4), 445–455.

Examples

# From a published fit table (no model object needed).
ecvi(chisq = 24.361, df = 8, npar = 13, multiplier = 301)
#>  term     value
#>  ecvi     0.167
#>  ci_lower 0.125
#>  ci_upper 0.243
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

fit <- lavaan::cfa(
  "visual =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t4_lozenges
   verbal =~ t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence + t9_word_meaning",
  data = holzinger_swineford, std.lv = TRUE)
ecvi(fit)
#>  term     value
#>  ecvi     0.167
#>  ci_lower 0.125
#>  ci_upper 0.243
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
